critical_steps: The two original families are identical Parseval fusion frames, so every weave has bounds one and one.
The rank-one map sends every basis line to the same nonzero closed line.
At the vector e_1, every transformed projection has norm one, so the transformed upper fusion sum diverges.
The cited upper-bound proposition in the source assumes the transformed families are already K-fusion Bessel sequences.
Adding transformed Bessel bounds restores the upper estimate while the source lower-bound argument supplies A/||K||^2.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact Hilbert-space construction on an orthogonal decomposition and a bounded rank-one operator.
integrity.unproved_limits: The repair is not asserted to be minimal, and no complete operator classification is proved.

scientific_limitations: The result refutes Proposition 2.5 as stated and isolates failure of the image-Bessel upper bound.
The proposed repair is sufficient: it assumes closed image subspaces and finite Bessel bounds for the two transformed families.
No necessary-and-sufficient characterization of all operators preserving image-subspace weaving is claimed.
title: A rank-one image collapse destroys the Bessel bound in a woven \(K\)-fusion construction
